what: The provenance ledger: one row per kind of figure in the UK register tables

kinds.counted: taken straight from an official UK register
kinds.worked out: our arithmetic on register figures, the method stated
kinds.looked up: a price or a rule read on a named page on a date (not in these tables)
kinds.estimate: our judgement where no register exists (not in these tables)

rows.figure: Businesses and premises per trade and borough
rows.source: ONS UK Business Counts (IDBR) via Nomis: NM_199_1 enterprises by industry and turnover band; NM_141_1 local units by industry and employment band
rows.data_date: March 2026 register snapshot; turnover is VAT-return turnover for the latest year the register holds
rows.attribution: Source: Office for National Statistics licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
leaves_out: registered businesses only: those registered for neither VAT nor PAYE (54% of UK businesses, most sole traders) are absent, so the median is the median of registered businesses and sits above the median of all
turnover is the enterprise's, counted at its registered address, so an area full of accountants' and formation agents' offices carries other areas' turnover
counts are rounded to the nearest 5 by the statistics office
where several trades share one SIC code, or a trade's code is only near it, the figure is the whole code's
the median is interpolated inside a turnover band on a log scale; neither it nor the quarter and tenth points are printed where an area holds under 40 enterprises (the register's own total)
the quarter and tenth points of sales are read the same way; one below 50k or above 50m rests on an assumed floor or ceiling, so it prints only as 'under 50k' or 'over 50m'

the range around the median is the lowest and highest median the true counts could give, each count being off by up to 2 because every whole count is rounded to the nearest 5 (the register is a census: rounding, not sampling, is its error); it does not cover where inside its band the median sits
a smooth curve fitted to the bands is kept only as a check and never printed: real takings are far from such a curve in most places, London restaurants most of all

rows.figure: How many new businesses are still trading after one to five years
rows.how: on the latest year's closure rates: each year's chance of closing, from the newest cohort with both ends of that year, applied in turn, with a 95% interval; the 2019 cohort's own five years beside it; the City of London never ranks
rows.source: ONS Business Demography, UK: 2024, reference tables (published 20 November 2025)
rows.data_date: published 20 November 2025: births 2019 to 2023, births and closures in 2024
rows.attribution: Source: Office for National Statistics licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
leaves_out: registered businesses only (VAT or PAYE)
a borough's survival is all trades together; the statistics office publishes no borough-by-trade cut
a trade's curve is its whole SIC group's, across the UK
counts are rounded to the nearest 5; percentages are recomputed from them

rows.figure: The official estimate of a year's rent per square metre, by kind of premises and borough
rows.source: Valuation Office Agency, Non-domestic rating: business floorspace, March 2025 (special category by local authority)
rows.data_date: 1 April 2021 (the 2023 rating list counted at 31 March 2025)
rows.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
leaves_out: rateable value estimates rent at the valuation date (April 2021), not today's asking rent
a category suppressed for a borough ([c]) or not present ([z]) prints nothing
many premises are valued in a general category: most salons and many cafes are valued as Shops
pubs and hotels are valued on receipts, not floorspace, and are absent

rows.figure: Company insolvencies a year per 1,000 live companies, per trade
rows.how: insolvency notices over twelve months, matched by company name to the register, over the trade's live companies, with a 95% interval; printed from 10 insolvencies in the year, marked few cases from 10 to 29
rows.source: The Gazette company insolvency notices (codes 2441, 2452, 2410 insolvent; 2431 solvent), published 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30; Companies House register snapshot 2026-05-01
rows.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 (company notices); Companies House register: no restrictions
rows.data_date: notices October 2025 to September 2026; register of 1 May 2026
rows.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
leaves_out: limited companies only; sole traders' insolvencies are personal data and are not counted
the per-1,000 rate divides by live, non-dormant companies of the trade on the May 2026 register
a notice whose company name does not match the register is left out (the match rate is printed)
the district is the registered office's
each rate per 1,000 live companies carries a 95% interval; it prints only where the year holds 10 or more insolvencies, and from 10 to 29 it is marked 'few cases'
